final.memo:
Our original engagement centered on correcting leadership, talent retention, and strategic drift, which has been materially addressed through the appointment of a new technical CEO and the rollout of the IDM 2.0 program [D07]. While the bear case warns of a capital-intensive turnaround that could strain cash flows, the latest results show execution is meeting or exceeding our expectations [D03, D05]. We acknowledge that the heavy manufacturing reinvestment cycle is a drag on near-term returns, but this is a necessary cost of the turnaround we advocated for [D03, D06].

We remain disciplined in our view that revenue growth alone is not the goal; we are tracking the actual cash conversion and the success of the new manufacturing roadmap [D06]. The board’s recent dividend increase is a welcome signal of capital discipline, though we will continue to monitor whether this competes unduly with essential capacity investments [D03]. At current valuation levels, the stock offers an attractive skew for patient investors as the market continues to discount the success of the turnaround [D04].

We maintain our position, as the catalyst remains active and the management team is currently executing on our core asks [D03, D07]. We will continue to evaluate the quarterly milestones of technical performance and free cash flow generation, holding the management team accountable to the specific goals of the IDM 2.0 plan [D03, D05].
